title: the trust claim does not absorb the callback's own inferred failure channel
notes: poc/src/language/README.md: "SMITHERS1303: an inferred-fallible function crosses a general callback boundary without an explicit Result contract." The callback ownership check never consults the boundary's trust, so it fires identically at a trusted call, an untrusted call, and a local higher-order call. This is one of the three cases that make the acceptance in 09-foreign-calls/a-callback-registered-through-a-trusted-binding-is-accepted narrow: the trust claim covers the call's panic channel and nothing else. The callback's own inferred Result channel, its started async work, and its body's authority are each owned by a rule that never reads the marker. THE SECOND DIAGNOSTIC IS GONE, and its absence is now part of what this case pins. Until 2026-08-30 this program also reported SMITHERS1204 at 12:39 for the `fallible(value)!` inside the callback body, because the old placement walk refused a `!` in a call argument. specification/failures.mdx §Refusal Conditions withdrew that walk (DECISIONS.md §Typed failures), and `sink.push(fallible(value)!)` is an unconditional, once-evaluated argument with nothing effectful to its left, so it is accepted and the callback-ownership rule is left as the only defect. That is the point of keeping the case: SMITHERS1303 never consulted the placement rule and must not have moved with it. A backend that reports both codes here is still enforcing the withdrawn walk. MARKER RETIRED 2026-08-30. The fork no longer reports the SMITHERS1204 at 12:39: its copy of the statement-walk is deleted and replaced by the reference's three predicates, and `sink.push(fallible(value)!)` satisfies none of them — the property read `sink.push` to the left of the argument leaves no effect behind for the hoisted guard to jump over. Measured on both backends; `compiler/fork_callback_trust_test.go` pins the same program with SMITHERS1303 as its only diagnostic.
